title: Efficient Deep Ensemble Inference via Query Difficulty-dependent Task Scheduling
motivation: Deep ensemble inference causes unacceptably high deadline miss rates in latency-sensitive tasks, reaching 45% during traffic bursts in real Q&A systems
problem_framing: Online scheduling problem: maximize inference accuracy under deadline constraints by dynamically selecting and scheduling base model inference tasks for each query
key_insight: 78.3% of samples can be correctly predicted by any single base model; only <11% require all models, indicating massive execution redundancy that can be eliminated via difficulty-aware scheduling
method_signature: Schemble uses discrepancy score (normalized distance to ensemble output) to predict query difficulty, then schedules base model tasks via DP-based algorithm considering queuing status
evaluation_criteria: Deadline miss rate and accuracy given deadline constraints, tested on text matching, vehicle counting, and image retrieval tasks
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: When all queries have similar difficulty (extreme easy or hard), the prediction module adds little value; DP(δ=0.001) incurs extra overhead causing higher miss rate
evidence_for_taste: deadline misses would reduce customer satisfaction and even be fatal

thinking_moves: Break ensemble inference into multiple independent base model tasks
Define novel discrepancy score instead of using ensemble agreement
Tackle scheduling via local subproblem DP when global optimal is intractable
Contrast system-level deadline constraint problem vs ML accuracy optimization
